倍低音薩魯梭風可在古典音樂與爵士錄音中聽見。古典編制裡，帕德雷夫斯基《波蘭尼亞》: The contrabass sarrusophone can be heard in classical music and on jazz recordings. In classical scoring, Paderewski's Symphony in B minor, 'Polonia', calls for three E-flat players, and the instrument is also used in Ravel's Rapsodie espagnole, Dukas's The Sorcerer's Apprentice, Debussy's Jeux, Bax's First Symphony, Stravinsky's Elegy and Childs's The Golden Bubble. On the jazz side, Bechet takes an E-flat solo on the 1924 recording of 'Mandy Make Up Your Mind'; on Kimbrough's 2018 album Monk's Dreams, Robinson plays the instrument on 'Misterioso' and 'Straight No Chaser'.
倍低音薩魯梭風是薩魯梭風家族中最大、音域最低的樂器，有降E、C、降B三種調性。傳: The contrabass sarrusophone is the largest and lowest-pitched instrument in the sarrusophone family, with instruments in E-flat, C and B-flat. It is traditionally played with a double reed, though a single-reed mouthpiece also exists; the reed is larger than a contrabassoon's and players often make their own. From the 19th century to the early 20th it was made mainly in France, with production also in Italy and the United States, where U.S. military bands used the E-flat instrument. Classical composers such as Ravel, Dukas and Debussy wrote for it, and Sidney Bechet and Scott Robinson are heard playing it on jazz recordings.
倍低音薩魯梭風為氣鳴樂器，是薩魯梭風家族最大、音域最低者，有降E、C、降B三種調: The contrabass sarrusophone is an aerophone and the largest, lowest-pitched member of its family, made in E-flat, C and B-flat. In the 19th century and the early 20th it was made mainly in France by the inventor, Pierre-Louis Gautrot, and by his successors Couesnon & Co. and Evette & Schaeffer; it was also made in Italy by Romeo Orsi and Rampone & Cazzani, and in the United States by C. G. Conn, which built E-flat instruments for U.S. military bands. Romeo Orsi, and Benedikt Eppelsheim in Germany, will still make them to order.
倍低音薩魯梭風為薩魯梭風家族中體積最大、音高最低者，有降E、C、降B三種調性。降: The contrabass sarrusophone is the bulkiest and lowest-pitched member of the sarrusophone family, made in E-flat, C and B-flat. The E-flat instrument sounds close to a contrabass saxophone with a reedier edge, and the C instrument close to a contrabassoon; the B-flat instrument is the lowest in the family and, until the E-flat octo-contra-alto clarinet, the B-flat octo-contrabass clarinet and the B-flat subcontrabass tubax appeared, was the lowest-pitched wind instrument. It sounds traditionally with a double reed, larger than a contrabassoon's, and a single-reed mouthpiece is also available. The source gives no information on how its volume is controlled.
演奏倍低音薩魯梭風時，先選擇適當簧片；傳統使用雙簧片，也可改用單簧片吹嘴。其簧片: To play the contrabass sarrusophone, first choose a suitable reed; a double reed is traditional, and a single-reed mouthpiece can be used instead. Its reed is larger than a contrabassoon's and can be made by the player or bought ready-made. The instrument stands about four feet tall and weighs roughly as much as a baritone saxophone, so a firm hold is the main thing. Begin by practising how to fit the reed and mouthpiece and how to hold the instrument steadily, then set the reed vibrating with a steady airstream.
